raw_response:
I am getting older, so I do not like taking big risks. On my 10.1 mu, I will still do the wheat-maize rotation like usual. That way the land does not stay idle, and even if one crop is not so good, I still have the other. I only finished primary school, so I mostly follow what has worked on my own fields and what the neighbors around me do. Wheat needs to be steady, so I will not cut fertilizer too much. If I save too much money there and the wheat turns yellow, then yield drops and I lose more. For maize, the time after wheat harvest is very tight, so I will keep it simple and plant quickly, probably with shallow tillage or direct seeding if I can get it done fast. Water from the well costs money, so I will irrigate when the crop really needs it, not too many times. I want a stable harvest more than chasing the very highest yield.
